note: hexloader reads Intel hex from the console and never times out - every download ends with an end-of-file record (:00000001FF), and a second hexloader is written, not sent: it waits for code and prints no prompt. It is on ukos-serial's unsafe list. The default (run) path used to jump to a NULL start address when a stale signature sat in the user memory (fixed, ../DEFECTS.md); a row asserts it now refuses.

then.await: ^Hex format Intel loader mode; waiting for the code\.$

tests.note: an end-of-file record alone is a complete, empty download. The second one must be accepted: hexloader used to keep the user memory reserved after every download, refusing all later ones until a reset (fixed, ../DEFECTS.md)

then.await: ^Hex format Intel loader mode; waiting for the code\.$

tests.note: the end-of-file record's checksum is FF; FE must be refused, and the failed download must give the user memory back

then.await: ^Hex format Intel loader mode; waiting for the code\.$

tests.note: the last checksum digit is G, so only the line end follows the refused character. A character that is not a hex digit used to read as 0 (fixed, ../DEFECTS.md); the next download must still be accepted

then.await: ^Hex format Intel loader mode; waiting for the code\.$

expect: ^Hex: failed to find the application signature!$

tests.note: without -norun, an end-of-file record alone leaves no start address: it must be refused. It used to jump to NULL whenever an earlier download had left a signature in the user memory, which SRAM keeps across resets - a HardFault (fixed, ../DEFECTS.md)
